title: cached_network_image
objectives: Understand cached_network_image via a real-life analogy
Cache network images on disk + memory correctly
Tune cache size + TTL via flutter_cache_manager

sections.markdown:
**Think of `cached_network_image` as `Image.network` with a photo album underneath.**

`Image.network(url)` fetches on every rebuild, decodes in the main isolate, and forgets the moment the widget disposes. On a scrolling feed with 200 thumbnails, this = 200 downloads, 200 decodes, jank + wasted bandwidth.

`CachedNetworkImage` solves it:
- **Two-tier cache** — in-memory `ImageCache` for the hot set (already decoded, ready to paint); on-disk cache (`flutter_cache_manager`) for the cold set (still avoids network, but has to decode).
- **Placeholder + error widgets** — first-class API; smooth UX without duct-taping FutureBuilders.
- **Progress builder** — for slow images with a real download bar.
- **HTTP cache-aware** — respects `Cache-Control` / `Expires` headers by default.
- **Custom cache manager** — bump TTL, cache size, storage location.
- **`fadeInDuration` / `fadeOutDuration`** — matches iOS-style fade transitions out of the box.

**Why every serious Flutter app uses this instead of `Image.network`:** on a real feed, cached_network_image cuts image download bandwidth 5-10× + eliminates re-decode jank. That's not premature optimization — it's the default.

**`cached_network_image`** wraps Flutter's `Image` with a two-tier cache: (1) Flutter's built-in `ImageCache` for decoded `ui.Image` objects, (2) `flutter_cache_manager` for on-disk file storage keyed by URL. Widgets: `CachedNetworkImage`, `CachedNetworkImageProvider` (for `ImageProvider` slots like DecorationImage). Config via `BaseCacheManager` — TTL, max cache size, custom file naming.

## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Not setting `memCacheWidth` / `memCacheHeight`.** Feed thumbnails decoded at full 4K = massive RAM + decode time. Set to the display size (multiply by devicePixelRatio if crisp).
**Mistake 2: Massive default cache.** 1000-image cache = disk full on entry-level devices. Cap via custom `CacheManager` (500 objects, 100 MB).
**Mistake 3: Ignoring `Cache-Control`.** Server sends `no-cache` → CachedNetworkImage still caches locally by default. If images are user-specific or short-lived, use signed URLs + evict on rotation.
**Mistake 4: No `errorWidget`.** Silent broken-image UX. Ship a fallback ALWAYS.
**Mistake 5: URL contains a rotating token.** Every rebuild → different URL → cache miss. Strip auth tokens; use signed URLs with sensible expiry.
**Mistake 6: Preloading too much.** `precacheImage` for 100 upcoming items = network storm + battery. Cap to next 5-10 above the fold.
**Mistake 7: Not clearing on logout.** Old user's images visible to new user on shared device. Wipe cache + ImageCache on logout.
**Mistake 8: Web target with CORS.** Some CDNs don't send CORS headers → CanvasKit throws taint errors → images fail silently on Flutter Web. Configure CDN correctly.
## Best practices
**1. Always `memCacheWidth`.** Match display size × devicePixelRatio.
**2. Custom `CacheManager` for feature-specific TTL** — hero images vs avatars vs thumbnails.
**3. Placeholder + error widgets** — mandatory.
**4. Preload sparingly** — 5-10 next images, not the whole list.
**5. Wipe cache on logout** — privacy + storage hygiene.
**6. Serve WebP / AVIF from CDN** — 30-50 % smaller vs JPEG at similar quality.
**7. Server-side image resizer** — Firebase Extensions Resize Images, Cloudinary, imgix — serve exactly the requested size.
**8. Test with `NetworkImage` mocked** for widget tests — no real network.

## Interview Q&A

**Q1: Why prefer `CachedNetworkImage` over `Image.network`?**

**A:** `Image.network` fetches + decodes on every rebuild of the widget (unless it's still in Flutter's `ImageCache`, which is small by default). For a scrolling feed with 200 thumbnails, that means 200 network round-trips per view + huge decode churn as tiles enter/leave the viewport. `CachedNetworkImage` adds an **on-disk cache via `flutter_cache_manager`**: URL → file. On the second view, no network — just disk read + decode. On the third view (still in memory), no decode either. Also gives you first-class `placeholder`, `errorWidget`, `progressIndicatorBuilder`, `fadeInDuration` — features you'd hand-roll with FutureBuilder otherwise. **On a real feed:** ~10× bandwidth reduction, ~3× lower jank.

**Q2: What is `memCacheWidth` and why does it matter?**

**A:** Without it, Flutter decodes the image at its FULL source resolution (say 4096×3072 for a 4K JPEG), keeps that in memory, then Scales at paint time. That's ~50 MB of RAM per image on a modest phone — devastate memory on a scrolling feed. `memCacheWidth: 400` (or `cacheWidth` on other providers) tells Skia/Impeller to decode at that width, discarding pixels beyond. **Rule:** set to `displayWidth * devicePixelRatio` — e.g., 100 px displayed × 3 devicePixelRatio = `memCacheWidth: 300`. **On a 20-tile grid**: full-res = 1 GB RAM; scaled = 60 MB. **Interviewer tip:** most candidates skip this; naming it puts you ahead.

**Q3: How do you configure a custom cache manager?**

**A:** `flutter_cache_manager` uses a `Config` object: `key` (namespace on disk), `stalePeriod` (TTL — how long before re-fetching), `maxNrOfCacheObjects` (LRU eviction cap), `fileService` (custom HTTP), `repo` (SQLite metadata DB). Subclass `CacheManager` + pass a `Config`; feed the manager into `CachedNetworkImage(cacheManager: MyManager())`. **Common tunings:** hero images = long TTL (30 days) + few objects (50); feed thumbnails = medium TTL (7 days) + many objects (500). **Storage caps** — check `flutter_cache_manager` doesn't grow the app sandbox unbounded; the LRU evicts oldest when count exceeded. **Wipe:** `manager.emptyCache()`; per-URL: `manager.removeFile(url)`. Interviewers love hearing about feature-specific managers.

**Q4: Preloading — when + how much?**

**A:** `precacheImage(provider, context)` warms the image into memory + disk before the widget is built. **Use when:** the user will imminently see the image — the next hero image, the next 5 feed tiles below the fold, the next carousel slide. **Do NOT preload 100 items** — network storm + battery drain + evicted memory forces re-fetches anyway. **Pattern:** in a list, on scroll, precache the next 5 items. Use a `PageStorageController` or a viewport listener. **Alternative:** rely on `CachedNetworkImage`'s own lazy fetch — for many apps, this is enough. **Interview tip:** knowing when NOT to preload is often the senior signal.

**Q5: How do you handle cache invalidation for changing content?**

**A:** **Rule of thumb: the URL is the cache key.** If the image content changes at the same URL, `CachedNetworkImage` won't know. **Solutions:** **(1) Cache-busting query param** — server includes `?v=<hash>` per version; new hash = new key = fresh fetch. **(2) Explicit evict** — after upload / edit, call `DefaultCacheManager().removeFile(url) + CachedNetworkImage.evictFromCache(url) + imageCache.evict(...)` for full clear. **(3) `Cache-Control: no-store`** — server-side header prevents caching (loses the whole benefit; use for user-specific dynamic images). **(4) TTL tuning** — accept some staleness; refresh every N days. **User avatar upload flow:** upload → get new URL (versioned) → save to DB → UI reads new URL → cache miss = fresh fetch. Interviewers score highly on 'versioned URLs' — the pragmatic answer.

**Q6: What can go wrong on Flutter Web?**

**A:** **(1) CORS issues.** If the image server doesn't send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, the browser blocks canvas taint checks — CanvasKit throws + image fails silently. Fix at the CDN, not in Flutter. **(2) No disk cache** — Web uses browser HTTP cache instead of `flutter_cache_manager`'s file store; TTL is browser-controlled. **(3) HTML renderer vs CanvasKit** — image handling differs; test both. **(4) Large images kill the tab** — WebGL memory limits are stricter than mobile GPU limits. **(5) HTTP/2 push** — reduces per-image RTT; enable at the CDN. **(6) WebP support universal now**; older browsers (IE — not a target since 2022 for most). **(7) `cacheWidth` still important** on Web — canvas decode isn't free.

## Real-world usage

- **Feeds** — every social / commerce / news app.
- **Product galleries** — with progress indicators for hero images.
- **Avatars** — small memCacheWidth, longish TTL.
- **NOT ideal for** — user-generated ephemeral images (Cache-Control: no-store); paid CDN-signed URLs with short expiry (evict on rotation).

## Advanced notes

- **`CachedNetworkImageProvider`** — for `DecorationImage`, `Ink.image`, `PhotoView`.
- **`filterQuality`** — Impeller has good defaults; override for hero images.
- **`useOldImageOnUrlChange`** — smoother URL-swap animations.
- **`imageBuilder`** — full custom widget with the decoded image (add shadow / mask / clip).
- **`fadeOutCurve` / `fadeInCurve`** — Cupertino-style feel.
- **Cache eviction hooks** — `CacheManager.getFileFromCache(url)` for manual read; test if hit.
- **Progress delta** — some servers don't send `Content-Length`; `progress` will be null.
- **`errorListener`** — global error tap for logging to Crashlytics.
- **`httpHeaders`** — attach auth tokens for private images (bearer tokens); careful about token in cache key.
- **`ExtendedImage`** — feature-richer alternative package.
- **`OctoImage`** — same author; simpler API + built-in variants (`OctoImage.wrapper`).
- **Sharing the on-disk cache with other packages** — `DefaultCacheManager` is a singleton; safe to use across `CachedNetworkImage`, `flutter_cache_manager` direct, etc.
